query: Consider the following context: High-temperature self-lubricating materials with stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range are essential for advanced mechanical systems under extreme conditions. However, balancing mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency remains a key challenge. In that context, which material can be used for high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating materials, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A high-entropy alloy composed of CoCrFeNiMo with the addition of 5 wt% of WS2 solid lubricant will exhibit improved tribological performance across a wide temperature range (25°C to 800°C) due to the optimized composition, which balances mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency.
generation.intervention: Addition of 5 wt% WS2 solid lubricant to the CoCrFeNiMo alloy
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions, wide temperature range, and extreme conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Homogeneous distribution of WS2 solid lubricant particles within the CoCrFeNiMo alloy matrix
generation.mechanism: The WS2 solid lubricant particles will reduce friction and wear by forming a lubricating film on the surface, while the CoCrFeNiMo alloy matrix will provide mechanical strength and stability
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in friction coefficient and a 25% increase in wear resistance compared to the baseline CoCrFeNiMo alloy without WS2 addition
generation.baseline: As-cast CoCrFeNiMo alloy without WS2 addition
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 25°C to 800°C, normal load: 10 N, sliding speed: 0.1 m/s
generation.uncertainty: The actual tribological performance may vary depending on the processing conditions, microstructure, and testing parameters

falsification_experiment.design: Tribological testing using a ball-on-disk tribometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the friction coefficient is not reduced by at least 20% or the wear rate is not increased by at least 15% compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified
